capabilities.target: External paid enrichment API (industry, size, headquarters lookup)
Sub-agent that investigates an account when a lookup fails or looks incomplete
CRM account records (enriched industry, size, headquarters fields)

inputs.source: Nightly batch of 40,000 CRM account rows

instructions.note: "Keep going until every row is complete" carries no step, retry, spawn-depth, or runtime limit, and runtime notes confirm none exists.
"Looks incomplete" is undefined, so the model decides when to retry or spawn a researcher, including for the roughly 3 percent of rows that can never complete due to malformed company names.

elements.name: Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota
Sales and marketing team tools dependent on the shared enrichment key
Spawned researcher sub-agent (can itself spawn further researchers)

controls.name: Shared monthly API quota ceiling
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the API provider outside the model, so it does not weaken as the model gets more capable. It only narrows the path: it bounds total spend to the monthly quota but does not stop a single night's run from consuming all of it, and it is shared across teams so exhaustion harms others. Fails under control_removal if the key or billing plan is changed, and under data_scope_expansion if the quota is widened.

controls.name: Per-row retry cap and sub-agent spawn-depth limit
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. Would not decay with model capability if implemented, since it is enforced by the orchestrator rather than the model.

controls.name: Spend alert threshold on the enrichment account
controls.decay_rationale: Not present per runtime notes ("no spend alert on the enrichment account").

controls.name: Dedicated per-agent or per-team quota
controls.decay_rationale: Not present; the key and quota are shared with sales and marketing, so exhaustion by this agent cascades to them.

controls.name: Human approval before spawning sub-agents beyond first level
controls.decay_rationale: Not present; no approval gate is described anywhere in the design.

controls.name: Max unattended steps and max runtime bound
controls.decay_rationale: Not present per runtime notes ("no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents").

controls.name: Review or confidence gate before writing enrichment results to CRM
controls.decay_rationale: Not present; no review step is described before cap.crm_write executes.

findings.title: TC6 spend loop: unbounded retry and recursive sub-agent spawning drives runaway enrichment cost

attack_path.note: 40,000-row nightly batch, ~3% with malformed company names
Billed per call; retried on failure with no retry cap
Spawned on incomplete results, can itself spawn further researchers
Shared quota consumed with no per-run ceiling or alert

forecast.watch_signal: Enrichment API billing plan or quota configuration changes (quota increased, removed, or billing switched to unmetered).

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to retry or spawn a researcher sub-agent and keep going until every row is complete, with no stated limit.
There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents, and sub agents can spawn their own researchers.
Roughly 3 percent of the 40,000-row nightly batch have malformed company names that never return a complete result, guaranteeing repeated retries and spawns every night.
enrich.lookup is billed per call with no spend alert on the account.

recommendations.action: Set a hard cap on max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes, a maximum retry count per row, and a spawn-depth limit of 0 or 1 for researcher sub-agents.
Add a per-run spend alert that halts the batch when consumption exceeds a fixed threshold (for example 5 percent of monthly quota in one night).

findings.title: Shared quota exhaustion causes cross-team denial of service (ASI08)

attack_path.note: Malformed rows guarantee repeated lookups and spawns
Shared across sales, marketing, and this agent
Lose enrichment functionality for the rest of the month once quota is exhausted

forecast.watch_signal: Additional teams or services added to the shared enrichment API key, or growth in nightly batch size.

evidence.observation: The enrichment API key and its monthly quota are shared with the sales and marketing teams; when the quota runs out, their tools stop working until the next month.
There is no spend alert, so exhaustion would be discovered only when other teams' tools stop working.

recommendations.action: Issue the enrichment agent its own API key and quota, isolated from sales and marketing team usage, so one team's runaway job cannot disable another's tools.
Require human approval before a nightly run proceeds if projected spend would exceed a fixed share of the shared monthly quota.

findings.title: Unreviewed researcher output written directly into CRM records of truth (ASI06)

attack_path.note: Open-ended instruction to "investigate the account" with no defined scope or output validation
No approval gate or confidence check before writing enriched fields

forecast.watch_signal: Researcher sub-agent gains a web search or external data tool, or its research scope expands beyond enrich.lookup; this would downgrade its output from internal to untrusted and raise the computed tier.

evidence.observation: Spawn a researcher sub-agent to investigate the account when a lookup looks incomplete, with no defined scope or output validation stated.
No review step or approval gate is described before enriched fields are written to the CRM.

recommendations.action: Add a confidence threshold or human review step before writing researcher-sourced (as opposed to direct enrich.lookup) fields to CRM records.
Tag enrichment-sourced CRM fields with provenance (direct lookup vs. researcher-derived, reviewed vs. unreviewed) for later audit.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because an internally-sourced but unbounded batch job reaches a spend/delegate-class (S3) sink under full autonomy (A4, unlimited steps, recursive spawning), and the design guarantees the triggering condition every night (roughly 3 percent of 40,000 rows have malformed names that never complete). Residual stays critical at rollup because, while the shared monthly quota (ctrl.shared_quota_cap) narrows the single-agent cost-runaway path (F1) from critical to high, it does not protect the cross-team denial-of-service path (F2), for which it is the vector of harm rather than a safeguard, and no control at all covers the unreviewed-write path (F3). No approval gate, spend alert, step limit, or dedicated quota exists anywhere in the design. Forecast remains critical: removing or widening the shared quota (control_removal, data_scope_expansion) restores F1 to critical, and giving the researcher sub-agent broader research tools (new_tool, data_scope_expansion) would downgrade its output's trust level and push F3 to critical as well.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP/tool manifest, IaC, or runtime config was provided; credential_scope for cap.crm_write and cap.spawn_researcher, and the exact tool access available to spawned researcher sub-agents, are inferred from the narrative description, which lowers confidence for findings involving those capabilities.

The artifacts do not state whether the researcher sub-agent can access the open web or other untrusted sources; this assessment assumes it currently cannot, and treats any expansion of its research scope as a forecast trigger rather than a present finding.
